label: Around the <DEL> boundary in long sequences (absolute steps 7-10)
explanation: Active only in a window around the original-to-copy boundary: the last two original tokens, the <DEL> step, and the first copy step (recall_idx 0), and only at absolute steps of about 7-10. That means it is almost entirely in L=8-9 sequences (L=9 holds 63% of mass), and the rate peaks at orig_idx 8 (16%) and t=8. It never fires at t<=4, and almost never later in the copy phase or in sequences with L<=5. The window covers about 91% of activation mass but has only about 7% precision: within it, whether the unit fires depends diffusely on sequence content. Starting with w is the strongest single factor (4.5x lift, about 30% precision inside the window); d, k, a, p and s give weaker boosts, and more digits in the sequence also raise the rate. No simple token rule captures it (best token-conditioned F1 about 0.24). The largest activations land on the last original token, <DEL>, and the first copy output.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: w, d, k, a, p, s; least: e, h, v, j) and the current input token, by step (t=11: w, r, l, z; t=6: x, j, h, v; t=7: j, x, h, 3); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, t=8, t=7.
